findings: GetTraceEnvVarOptions selects actual Environment options when nonnull, otherwise actual per_process cli_options->per_isolate->per_env. It snapshots message, JS stack and native stack flags into a by-value local.

TraceEnvVarImpl performs selected fprintf(stderr) first, selected DumpNativeBacktrace(stderr) second, then selected DumpJavaScriptBacktrace(stderr). There is no explicit flush, pending-reason capture, TryCatch, clear, throw, or terminal operation in TraceEnvVarImpl.
The const-char message and const-char key overloads invoke that helper even when message output is disabled, so a selected native or JS stack still runs.

The Local<String> key overload encloses Utf8Value construction AND the entire helper call in print_message. When print_message is false this original overload does not invoke either stack, even if its stack flags are true.
DumpNativeBacktrace prints the native header, captures up to256 frames, skips index0, emits numbered address/name lines and has no fflush call.

DumpJavaScriptBacktrace returns without output for no current isolate or an empty/unavailable captured stack. Its capture uses GetCurrentStackTrace's original default frame count, not a count chosen by this packet.

GetCurrentStackTrace returns empty for recursive capture, native is_in_oom, or no entered context. It sets its native thread-local reentry flag around intrinsic CurrentStackTrace using an EscapableHandleScope.

For a nonempty JS stack, DumpJavaScriptBacktrace writes its leading/header lines, calls PrintStackTrace(...kNumber), then writes one trailing newline. PrintStackTrace alone routes through FPrintF(stderr,"%s\n",formatted) followed by fflush(stderr). The final DumpJavaScriptBacktrace newline occurs after that flush and is not explicitly flushed again.

The original trace path does not read guest Error.stack, call a guest formatter, or deliberately consume/replace an existing ordinary pending reason. The captured-stack entry is ENTER_V8_NO_SCRIPT_NO_EXCEPTION. Actual native allocation failure/termination policy is separate and must not be converted into a fabricated guest reason or suppressed by a generic pending bypass.

The selected Environment path ABI already carries required nonterminal native_stack(user) and js_stack(user,JSContext*) operations. Both are called for stderr semantics; no report/abort/default noop is supplied. The actual original default frame count and lower capture allocation policy remain the shared diagnostic owner's retained dependencies.
